To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the HQs are equally dragged by the kinetically and thermally equilibrated gluonic systems; and (ii) the HQs diffuse faster in the pre-thermalization stage than in the chemially equilibrated quarks and gluons.

(1) the heavy quarks (both charm and beauty) are dragged almost equally in the pre-equilibrated gluons as in the kinetially equilibrated gluonic system, and (2) the heavy quark diffusion is faster in both kinetically and chemically equilibrating gluonic systems than in the chemially equilibrated quarks–gluons plasma
the HQ diffusion is faster in out-of-equilibrium than in chemically equilibrating gluonic systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the heavy quarks produced in the pre-equilibrated phase of the fireball produced in the heavy ion collisions.
the study of the transport properties of the heavy quarks in the hot and dense matter produced in heavy ion reactions at the relativistic heavy ion collision and the large hadron collider energies.
the study of heavy quark diffusion in pre-equilibrium gluons produced during the first few fm/c of heavy ion collisions at RHIC and LHC energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HQ diffusion and drag coefficients in the pre-equilibrated gluon phase are almost equal to the ones in the kinetically and chemically equilibrated quark–gluin plasma phase.
the pre-equilibrium dynamics has a nontrivial role in the transport of heavy quarks.
HQ diffusion in the early stage of heavy ion collision is not much affected by the fact that the produced gluons are out of thermal equilibrium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HQ diffusion coefficient in the pre-equibration stage is larger than that in the quark–glul plasma phase.
the HQs interact almost equally with the kinetically equilibrate and out-of-equilibrate gluonic systems and the diffusion in the out-of-equilibra is faster than in the chemical equilibrium.
the HQ diffusion is not sensitive to the initial conditions and it is as fast as the equilibrated QGP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pre-equilibrium evolution of the fireball should be included in the theoretical analysis of the experimental data.
the pre-equilibrium evolution of the fireball is as important as the thermalization process in the evolution of the fireballs produced in heavy ion colliders.
the diffusion coefficients of the HQs in the pre-equilibrated gluonic medium can be used as initial conditions in the dynamical simulations of the heavy ion collisions.
